title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by providing safe, autosuggested defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, shipping curated quantization profiles, and adding unit-economics tooling so teams can see cost impact before rollout. This PR wires together three pieces: 1) autotune heuristics that pick batching/caching defaults based on per-route latency SLOs and request-size distribution; 2) a small set of tested quantization profiles (int8/ptq-friendly) and compatibility checks for runtime; 3) a UI + CLI unit-economics surface that simulates expected cost/latency tradeoffs for a given route and traffic shape. Summary of changes: - runtime/autotune: implement fallback-safe batching policy generator, prefix-KV cache defaults, and admission checks when latency SLOs are tight. - runtime/kernels: add checks for quant-profile compatibility and a new small quant table for int8-ptq tuned for A100/GPU families. - optimize/service: add /v1/optimize/preview endpoint to estimate tokens-per-second, estimated monthly cost, and delta vs baseline. - console: add a Cost Preview widget on the Route settings page and a CLI flag --preview-cost. - tests: integrate new unit and perf tests; add a small synthetic benchmark harness for preview accuracy. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by infra and runtime teams (ENG-4123) - [x] Integration tests for autotune heuristics - [x] E2E cost-preview smoke tests - [x] Updated docs and Console UI strings - [x] Backwards compatible runtime changes How this behaves in production: New routes will get suggested batching/caching defaults during route creation; teams can preview unit economics and opt-in to apply defaults. Autotune runs off a snapshot of traffic distribution and will never increase batch sizes beyond a route's configured latency SLO. Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature flag rts.autotune.batching and staged canary to 10% of new routes first; full rollout after 48h of canary telemetry. Related: ENG-4123, ENG-4189, SUP-1024.

review_comments: Marco Li: Overall looks good. A couple of nits on naming and one functional question: what prevents batching from increasing tail latency for short requests?

Anika Patel: Reply: autotune uses per-route latency SLO and simulated P99 from the snapshot; we cap batch size based on SLO and observed headroom. Added comments and a unit test for short-request workloads.
Samir Kapoor: Please add a compatibility check to ensure quant profiles don't get applied to models with unsupported ops (e.g., custom kernels).
Anika Patel: Added runtime compatibility checks and a failing test case for a custom op; falls back to fp16 profile if incompatibility is detected.
Riley Chen: CI flakiness on the perf harness; observed intermittent 5-7% variance that caused a false negative. Recommend stabilizing seeding and increasing run iterations.
Anika Patel: Addressed: harness now seeds RNG and uses median over 5 runs. CI rerun green.
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, ship curated quantization profiles with runtime compatibility checks, and introduce a Unit Economics Cost Preview (Console + CLI + API). This improves default unit costs for typical chat and completion workloads and provides tooling to preview cost/latency tradeoffs before applying changes.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated under rts.autotune.batching. Canary rollout plan included; monitor p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per 1M tokens. If tail latency increases >5% for canary routes, rollback flag rts.autotune.batching immediately.
